settings.phantom_preview.caption.text: Phantom preview (setup pose; back on support pad/table). Reflects body-habitus scales and patient offsets (active exam when multiple exams are loaded). Display uses a reduced mesh for speed; dose calculation and Geometry setup/event plots use the full mesh.

per_exam.tx_tz_swap.tooltip.text: Manual extra swap only; GE RDSR-level correction is handled during normalization.

export.include_identifiers.explanation.text: Off by default. Enable only when an identified clinical record is intentionally required.

upload.privacy_notice.text: Privacy: filenames and file contents may contain PHI. Uploads are copied to a private random-name session directory and removed on clear or shutdown.

onboarding.intended_use.text: GUISkinDose is not FDA-cleared or otherwise certified as a medical device. It is intended for research, education, development, and institutional quality assurance, and its results are not independently validated for patient-care decisions. Qualified medical physicists and physicians are responsible for reviewing its inputs and outputs, evaluating patient skin dose, and making any clinical decisions.

results.intended_use.text: Not FDA-cleared. Skin dose estimates must be reviewed by a qualified medical physicist or physician.

results.psd_band.low.text: Low — peak skin dose below 5000 mGy

results.psd_band.elevated.text: Elevated — peak skin dose 5000 to just under 10000 mGy

results.psd_band.high.text: High — peak skin dose 10000 mGy or above

onboarding.privacy_notice.text: Processing and temporary upload storage stay on this machine. The GUI binds localhost only and refuses any other host — it will not serve other machines by itself, so do not expose it with a proxy; move the computation to the machine where the data may reside instead. Loopback binding is not an authentication boundary. Browser access needs the console launch URL (it bootstraps your session and stays valid until restart) or an active session on this machine — anyone with either sees the same shared state, so shared workstations need their own access story. Strict Host/Origin checks block cross-site pages and rebinding tricks, and in browser mode every request and socket needs the session (native mode skips the token check). Source filenames and data may contain PHI. Upload copies use private random session names and are removed on clear or shutdown; crash leftovers are removed after 24 hours. Exports can be clinical records, so choose an approved destination and retention policy.

kerma.dialog.body.text: Enter CF = (real measured dose) / (unit reported dose) for each unit and tube of each exam. Exam 2 and later follow the previous exam until you change them, so a recalibrated meter can have a different factor per exam. Rows marked "default" have no entered or file value, so please review them. Cancel keeps file values and earlier entries, and unanswered pairs use the default factor.

kerma.dialog.unresolved.text: No equipment identity was found for this exam. Choose or type the unit it was acquired on so its factors can be looked up.

kerma.dialog.dont_ask.text: Don't ask again until the loaded data changes

settings.kerma_meter.ask_missing.tooltip.text: Open a dialog when a detected unit and tube has no entered or file factor. Never blocks a calculation.

kerma.dialog.error_invalid.text: Enter a number greater than zero for every factor, or press Cancel.

kerma.dialog.stale_discarded.text: The loaded data changed while the dialog was open, so your entries were discarded. Open Review correction factors to enter them again.

kerma.review.unavailable.text: Turn on kerma-meter correction and load events first.

settings.k_tab.info.text:
**Checked (estimated).** One flat factor, `k_tab_val` (default 0.8), is used for every event. It is applied only to skin cells whose beam passes through the table or pad.

**Unchecked (measured).** Each event is looked up in the bundled measured table by scanner model and tube. The lookup uses kVp and Cu/Al filtration, with interpolation.

If the model or tube is unknown, or data are missing, the factor falls back to 1.0. That means no table attenuation, and a warning is shown.

The measured data cover only a few models. On other equipment, unchecking usually removes table attenuation instead of improving accuracy.
